specialist: cross-branch leakage + tamper of stock_movements + auth on dashboard
summary: BranchScope applied to BOTH StockLevel and StockMovement models — cross-branch read leakage closed via global scope (iter12 P0). Service writes are all sourced from order.branch_id, and StockService rejects branch_id<=0. Dashboard controller uses permission-gated scopedBranches() respecting user branch_id. AvailabilityService::decrementForOrder has one raw-SQL site with $qty interpolated — cast to int just before, so technically safe but worth flagging since it's the lone raw-SQL hot path. Two security-adjacent concerns: (1) DB-level append-only enforcement gap (see DBA F6-DBA-01) means a compromised admin with DB ACCESS can tamper stock_movements without breaking the audit chain; (2) idempotency_key is a sha1 of predictable order/line composite — not security-sensitive (it's just a dedup key), but an attacker who can submit crafted X-Idempotency-Key headers could theoretically pre-compute and pre-claim a movement key. Not a current attack surface.

findings.title: stock_movements tamper window — DB-level append-only missing, audit chain not HMAC-signed
findings.primary_source: Compared to audit_logs (HMAC chain + DB trigger) and z_reports (HMAC chain). stock_movements has NEITHER — no HMAC prev_hash → current_hash chain, no DB BEFORE DELETE trigger. Migration creates only idempotency UNIQUE.
findings.impact: An attacker with DB write privilege (compromised admin user, MySQL root via privilege escalation) can DELETE individual rows or UPDATE delta values without leaving any forensic trace. NF525-grade integrity claims for fiscal sequences do not extend to stock. A reconciliation of orders vs stock_movements can produce misleading totals if movements are silently doctored. Reconciliation must therefore rely on order_items + composition_snapshot (which IS chain-signed via audit_logs) rather than stock_movements alone.
findings.user_friendly_question: Owner — stock_movements n'a ni HMAC chain ni trigger DB BEFORE DELETE. Audit_logs et z_reports en ont. Si un admin compromis (ou DBA accidentel) modifie/supprime des lignes stock_movements, aucune détection. Pour V1 Le Cayenne single-resto + 1 admin de confiance, c'est acceptable. Pour V2 SaaS multi-tenant, ça devient un risque. Veux-tu (1) ajouter trigger DB en V1.0.1 (heal-light, voir DBA F6-DBA-01), (2) ajouter HMAC chain (lourd, ~30 LOC + migration + tests), ou (3) accepter le risque V1 et tracker en V2 backlog?
findings.remediation_proposal: V1 minimal: add BEFORE DELETE trigger (couples with F6-DBA-01). V2 escalation: add prev_hash + current_hash columns + HmacService::sign sur chaque insert; verify chain command similar à FiscalVerifyChainCommand. ROI lower than fiscal chain (no legal mandate) but useful for SaaS forensic.
findings.keep_current_working: Today single-resto + trusted admin = minimal risk. Heal recommended for V1.0.1.

findings.title: AvailabilityService::decrementForOrder L310-312 raw SQL with {$qty} interpolation
findings.primary_source: L294: `$qty = (int) $line->quantity;` — cast to int before L310 `DB::raw("CASE WHEN daily_consumed_qty + {$qty} > max_daily_qty THEN max_daily_qty ELSE daily_consumed_qty + {$qty} END")`.
findings.impact: Safe as written — the (int) cast prevents SQL injection. But the pattern (raw SQL with string interpolation) is the only such site in the Stock/Availability surface; if a future refactor changes the cast or switches $qty to a string from a non-trusted source, injection becomes possible. PR review burden / static-analysis blind spot.
findings.user_friendly_question: Owner — le seul raw SQL avec interpolation dans Stock+Availability est AvailabilityService L310. Aujourd'hui sécurisé via (int) cast L294. Veux-tu (1) refactor en query builder + bindings (plus de garanties), (2) ajouter un commentaire défensif + Psalm/PHPStan strict-type, ou (3) laisser tel quel?
findings.remediation_proposal: Refactor: use DB::table('item_branch_availability')->update(['daily_consumed_qty' => DB::raw('LEAST(daily_consumed_qty + ?, max_daily_qty)'), ...]) with bindings. Equivalent semantics in MySQL/SQLite (LEAST + COALESCE for MySQL).

findings.title: BranchScope global scope coverage verified for both Stock models
findings.primary_source: Both models call `static::addGlobalScope(new BranchScope())` in their boot(). Comments document iter12 P0 STOCK 2026-05-09 rationale.
findings.impact: Cross-tenant read leakage closed. Multi-branch admin (branch_id=0) bypass preserved. Staff scoped per their user.branch_id automatically.

findings.title: Dashboard authz uses permission gates + authorizeWritableBranchScope on POST
findings.primary_source: L23-25: permission:items_show on read endpoints, permission:items_create on run. L196-201 authorizeWritableBranchScope + production-mode hard guard. scopedBranches L221-244 restricts non-admin users to their branch_id.
findings.impact: Acceptable. Authz layered correctly. One nit: L199 `app()->environment('production')` adds extra can-check only in prod; staging/dev permissions less strict. Probably intentional for QA, but worth noting.

cross_branch_leakage_check.verdict: Both stock models have BranchScope. Pre-iter12 leak closed.

tamper_resistance.db_level: MISSING — no trigger, no HMAC chain
tamper_resistance.compare_audit_logs: audit_logs has BOTH (trigger + HMAC chain). stock_movements has neither.

raw_sql_sites.verdict: Safe today, fragile pattern. P2 refactor.

idempotency_key_attacker_model.key_formula: sha1(reason | order::class | order.id | line_uid | stockable_type | stockable_id [| seed]) — see StockService::movementKey
idempotency_key_attacker_model.attacker_can_predict: Yes — all inputs are publicly observable or guessable per order context
idempotency_key_attacker_model.exploitation: An attacker who knows an order's pending decrement could insert a stock_movement with the predicted idempotency_key (if they had write access to stock_movements, which is admin-only). Not an external attack surface. Internal-only.
idempotency_key_attacker_model.verdict: Not a current threat. Idempotency_key is a dedup mechanism, not a security secret.
